content: {"decision":"Reject current behavior: four leases do not bound running calls when calls outlive leases or controllers independently reuse capacity.","risks":["Redis outages let both controllers admit work without shared accounting.","Lease expiry permits replacement calls while previous calls remain active; repeated expiry can cause unbounded concurrency.","Controller restarts or ambiguous launch outcomes can hide running calls and enable duplicate work."],"required_changes":["Fail closed on unavailable or uncertain quota state; keep existing and uncertain calls charged against capacity.","Enforce an atomic global admission limit of four. Release capacity only after confirmed completion or confirmed termination; lease expiry alone must not release a running call's slot.","Use unique call IDs, idempotent admission and launch, and ownership-checked release. Reconcile outstanding calls before admitting work after recovery.","Enforce execution deadlines and cancellation at the execution service; a local timeout is not proof of termination. Fencing must be enforced where work executes and must prevent overlap before slot reuse.","If outage availability is required, preassign disjoint controller budgets totaling at most four, including surviving and uncertain calls; prohibit borrowing or reassignment without confirmed quiescence.","Bound waiting queues and retries; reject excess demand with backoff."],"evidence_needed":["Fault tests covering Redis partitions, lease expiry during long calls, delayed cancellation, ambiguous launches, controller restarts, and Redis failover.","Execution-side traces showing actual concurrent calls never exceed four throughout failures and recovery, rather than merely counting leases.","Verified atomic admission, durable outstanding-call accounting, idempotency, stale-release protection, and execution-side termination or fencing semantics."]}
